reason: The text depicts active expression of views and emotions by the characters. Cain expresses his anger (וַיִּ֤חַר לְקַ֙יִן֙ מְאֹ֔ד - 'Cain was very angry'), God directly addresses his feelings (וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־ קָ֑יִן - 'And the LORD said to Cain'), and Cain explicitly complains to God about his judgment (גָּד֥וֹל עֲוֺנִ֖י מִנְּשֹֽׂא - 'My punishment is too great to bear'). While Cain's expressions do not prevent his punishment, they are clearly permitted and even acknowledged by God through direct dialogue. The narrative demonstrates open communication and expression rather than discouragement from voicing one's views.
